newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to slash taxes in reforms package.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to slash taxes in reforms package.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government on Friday unveiled an economc reforms package which slashed a range of taxes.

The package, announced by Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz in a speech to the National Assembly (lower house of parliament), included cuts in the maximum import tariff to 45 percent from the existing 65 percent, except automobiles.
It would also reduce the general sales tax and personal income tax.
The standard general sales tax (GST) would be cut to 12.5 percent from the existing 18 percent, and personal income tax rates to a range of five to 20 percent from 10 to 35 percent.
Aziz also proposed a three percent general sales tax (GST) at the retail level to begin on July 1, initially in large cities, including the capital Islamabad.
Details of the tax would be discussed with traders, but the sale of food items and medicines would be exempt, he said.
The package would form the basis for proposed negotiations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for an Extended Structural Adjustment Fund loan, Aziz said.
"By bringing down the general level of tariffs we hope to improve the relative profitability of investments in export-oriented sectors," he said.
"Reduction of tariffs on industrial raw materials will stimulate industrial production."

"Any potential loss of revenues is being compensated for by measures like the introduction of a minimum tariff of 10 percent on imports and by recovering the revenues currently foregone due to the concessionary (orders)," he added.
Karachi Stock Exchange president Arif Habib said welcomed the package.
"The overall impact of lower taxes as proposed by the Finance Minister will be positive on the industry," he said.
He said the cuts in corporate taxes, the general sales tax and income taxes would boost corporate profits.
